hints.title: Subtree Coin Balance Tracking
hints.text: For any subtree, its net excess or deficit of coins must pass through the edge connecting it to its parent.

hints.title: Edge Flow Formula
hints.text: The net balance of a subtree is node.val + left_balance + right_balance - 1. The absolute value of this balance is the number of coin moves across that edge.

hints.title: Post-Order Accumulation
hints.text: Perform post-order traversal. For null nodes return 0. Recursively compute left and right balance. Add abs(left) + abs(right) to total moves. Return node.val + left + right - 1. Return total moves at root.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def distributeCoins(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
        moves = 0
        def dfs(node: Optional[TreeNode]) -> int:
            nonlocal moves
            if not node:
                return 0
            left = dfs(node.left)
            right = dfs(node.right)
            moves += abs(left) + abs(right)
            return node.val + left + right - 1
        dfs(root)
        return moves
```

variables: N: number of nodes in binary tree
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating individual coin movements step by step introduces complex graph flow logistics.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since trees have unique paths between all nodes, edge flow is uniquely determined by subtree balance, running in O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should show that net subtree surplus/deficit must cross the parent edge regardless of target node destinations.
complexity.notes: Every node ultimately retains exactly 1 coin.
